text.p: Elections in Russia's Chechnya republic for a president and a legislative assembly on Monday mark a key date in the region's long resistance to Russian rule, culminating in a 21-month war against Moscow.
1859 - The North Caucasus region of Chechnya is incorporated into the Russian empire after nearly half a century of fighting led by legendary Imam Shamil.
1870 - The regional capital Grozny is founded.
1944 - Soviet dictator Josef Stalin deports the entire Chechen people to Central Asia, accusing them of collaboration with Nazi Germany. Tens of thousands die.
1957 - Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev allows the Chechens back to the Caucasus, where the Checheno-Ingush ethnic republic is set up.
Oct 1991 - Following the overthrow of local communist ruler Doku Zavgayev, Soviet air force general Dzhokhar Dudayev wins a disputed local poll and declares Chechnya independent.
Nov 1991 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin declares a state of emergency in the territory and sends troops to Grozny. They pull out after a few hours.

Summer/Autumn 1994 - Russia accuses Dudayev of allowing Chechnya to become a haven for terrorists and urges the Chechens to topple him. Moscow gives covert military support to anti-Dudayev opposition attempts to overthrow him but an armed assault on Grozny fails.
Dec 1994 - Russia sends troops to Chechnya to crush Dudayev's independence movement but they meet strong resistance and suffer heavy casualties.
Jan 1995 - Russian troops storm central Grozny after tank, artillery and rocket bombardments reduce much of it to ruins.
Feb 1995 - Separatists abandon Grozny.
March 1995 - The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) sets up a mission in Chechnya.

June 1995 - About 100 rebels, led by guerrilla commender Shamil Basayev, storm the southern Russian town of Budennovsk and seize hundreds of hostages in a raid in which scores of people are killed. Peace talks open and Russia orders a halt to military operations in Chechnya. But the conflict goes on.
Dec 1995 - Russian-backed leader Doku Zavgayev wins an election widely dismissed as fraudulent to head Chechnya's administration.

Jan 1996 - Chechen fighters led by Salman Raduyev seize hostages in neighbouring Dagestan, then move to the settlement of Pervomaiskoye just outside Chechnya. Most of the rebels escape after a four-day stand-off with Russian troops but scores are killed.
Feb 1996 - Yeltsin says the Chechnya campaign was "maybe one of our mistakes". He says he is studying options for peace but rules out withdrawal of Russian forces or massive use of force.

March 1996 - Rebels attack Grozny and hold some areas for several days. Yeltsin announces a halt to wide-scale military action, a partial withdrawal of troops and an offer of indirect talks with the rebels. But the fighting continues.
April 1996 - Dudayev is reported killed in a rocket attack and replaced by vice-president Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev.
May 1996 - Yeltsin and Yandarbiyev agree a truce at talks in Moscow. It holds for about six weeks until the Russian presidential election. Yeltsin visits Russian troops in Grozny.

Aug 1996 - Chechen rebels infiltrate Grozny and seize control of the city. Yeltsin gives national security adviser Alexander Lebed power to resolve the crisis. Lebed signs a peace deal on August 31 providing for a Russian troop pullout and deferring the issue of Chechen sovereignty for five years.
Sept 1996 - Russia starts withdrawing its soldiers.
Oct 1996 - Aslan Maskhadov, the rebel chief-of-staff during the fighting, is named prime minister of an interim government pending January elections.
Dec 1996 - Six Red Cross workers are murdered in the Chechnya, casting a shadow over the election campaign.
Jan 1996 - Sixteen candidates run for president, but three drop out just before the poll.
